title: The Water Cycle
author: USGS VizLab and Water Science School; Corson-Dosch, Nell, Volentine, Archer, Bechtel, Bruce, Felts, Gross, Lopez-Trujillo, Riggs, and Read
license_observation: The USGS image page explicitly marks this media as Public Domain. The downloaded filename records a 2023-03-02 revision.
figure: Complete English landscape cutaway and footer explanations; source original 11400×7800 pixels.
object_count_basis: Twenty named water pools and human-use sites represented as native nodes. Terrain, weather, landscape structures, and repeated flux marks add many visual objects beyond this deliberately limited principal count.
reading_path: Read the atmospheric band and precipitation, scan the mountain-to-ocean landscape, then the subsurface cutaway. The legend and footer explain storage, movement, human use, water quality, and climate.
merit: A pale terrain block allows saturated blue water to stand out. Geographic position, depth, repeated directional flux marks, italic process labels, and compact explanatory prose integrate natural and human systems.
preview_note: Original 11400×7800 raster retained; 1800×1232 preview is a full proportional reduction. Dense labels require the original or detail crop.
